## Laboratory 04 - Step 1/4

**Goal:** Add one valid-subnet test and one intended invalid-CIDR rejection. The complete baseline, security child and mocks are supplied; no earlier lab is needed.

**Work:** your private copy's root, branch `lab/tests-docs`.
**File:** edit [tests/learner.tftest.hcl](../../tests/learner.tftest.hcl) from the [supplied starter](../../exercises/learner-test.tftest.hcl.example); leave module code unchanged.

[Setup/accounts](../../docs/start-here.md) · [Git help](../../docs/git-workflow.md) · [Toolchain](../../docs/toolchain.md) · [Recovery](../../docs/troubleshooting.md)

### Do 1 — Prepare this copy once

Already in your copy or Exercise? **Do not copy again.** Otherwise follow the [landing page](../../README.md) to install tools, sign in, copy privately, clone and open that clone in desktop VS Code. Complete account/Copilot and local Git authorship checks.

From the clean actual default branch (normally `dev`), **Pull**, then **Git: Create Branch...** → `lab/tests-docs`, or select the existing branch. In **Terminal → New Terminal** at the root, run separately:

```powershell
node --version
terraform version
terraform-docs version
node scripts/doctor.mjs
```
**Why:** Version commands report installed tools; the doctor checks local readiness, not authentication or a Copilot seat. **Expect:** Node **24.16.0**, Terraform **1.16.1**, terraform-docs **0.24.0**, and the supplied AzureRM **5.4.0** pin/lock. Resolve every doctor `CHECK` or missing tool through setup before proceeding.

### Do 2 — Write both complete cases

Replace the comment-only learner scaffold with the supplied starter below. Keep the [synthetic-ID mock fixtures](../../tests/mocks/network.tfmock.hcl), default inputs and exact run names; remove `TODO` and save:

```hcl
mock_provider "azurerm" {
  source          = "./tests/mocks"
  override_during = plan
}

variables {
  name                = "ws2-network"
  resource_group_name = "rg-ws2-existing"
  location            = "southeastasia"
  address_space       = ["10.42.0.0/16"]
  subnets = {
    web  = { address_prefixes = ["10.42.1.0/24"] }
    data = { address_prefixes = ["10.42.2.0/24"] }
  }
  tags = { owner = "team", environment = "dev", cost_center = "training", workshop = "ws2" }
}

run "learner_valid_subnets" {
  command = plan
  assert {
    condition     = toset(keys(output.subnet_ids)) == toset(["web", "data"])
    error_message = "Both named subnets must be present."
  }
}

run "learner_reject_invalid_cidr" {
  command = plan
  variables {
    address_space = ["not-a-cidr"]
  }
  expect_failures = [var.address_space]
}
```

The rejection passes because `var.address_space` rejects malformed CIDR syntax, not because login, provider setup or another validation fails. Do not change guards, add real providers/aliases or redirect the tested module.

### Do 3 — Execute both cases

At the root, run separately and stop on unexpected errors:

```powershell
terraform fmt -check -recursive
terraform init -backend=false -lockfile=readonly -input=false
terraform validate
terraform test '-filter=tests\learner.tftest.hcl'
```
**Why:** Check formatting recursively; download locked dependencies with backend disabled, lock read-only and prompts off; validate; then select the learner file. **Expect:** **two executed passes**, including the intended rejection. Fix the first diagnostic rather than weakening a check.

On macOS/Linux replace only the last line:

```bash
terraform test '-filter=tests/learner.tftest.hcl'
```
**Why:** Native separators matter: Windows needs backslashes; macOS/Linux uses slashes. **Expect:** the same two passes. Quote the whole argument; `Unknown test file` or zero/skipped tests is not success, even with exit 0. Check the path and saved content.

### Do 4 — Save and advance

**Save → stage → commit → push → refresh the SAME Exercise.** Review the learner-test diff; use `lab: add valid subnet and invalid CIDR tests` and **Publish Branch** for the first push. See [Git help](../../docs/git-workflow.md).

Inspect **Actions → Lab checks → newest commit → Test learner module**. AgentAlvine checks both named runs, the mock, output assertion and intended failure target. Full CI can remain red until the later fixture/docs edits; keep those gates.

No Azure login, backend/state access or real plan/apply. Counts above are expectations to confirm in actual output, not a new test result.
